originality.rationale: The precise new invariant is the complete cardinality-refined polynomial sequence for open ladders. Dourado et al. (2026) establish general counting complexity and methods but do not state this bivariate ladder series in their inspected full HTML. The unweighted ladder sequence, its order-five recurrence and its generating function are ALREADY KNOWN in OEIS A231376 (2013/2018) and are not claimed as new; the scalar evaluation at z=1 does not imply the coefficient distribution for arbitrary z. Searches against bootstrap/strict-majority aliases, the relevant primary papers, published-finding corpus and current accessible own claims revealed no full bivariate formula. An unindexed equivalent remains possible.
residual_risks: An earlier bivariate weighted strict-majority-array enumerator may exist outside searchable indexed sources.
The 2013 OEIS scalar recurrence is decisive prior art and must never be relabeled a new finding.
The bootstrap literature contains structurally related fixed-point results; the full content of every older paper was not exhaustively inspected.
No independent mathematical audit has been performed.

value.rationale: Counting closed configurations by cardinality answers the natural size-conditioned question for two-neighbor percolation, rather than just totaling configurations. The complete polynomial distribution is not determined by OEIS scalar counts, and the nonobvious ten-state symmetry reduction yields a short order-five polynomial-coefficient recurrence for every length. This is a motivated exact infinite-family refinement of a #P-hard general counting problem; it does not depend on the scalar result being original.
